overview: The Medford Public Schools (MPS) School Committee serves as the governing body for the district, responsible for policy formulation, budget approval, labor contract ratifications, curriculum selection, and facilities oversight. Across the record spanning May 2023 through October 2026, the committee navigated significant district administrative transitions, major HVAC and infrastructure remediation across aging school buildings, and preliminary design phases for a comprehensive high school building project. The body routinely coordinates with city departments, state education officials, and student advisory groups to align district policy with community needs. At its most recent meetings, the committee selected ground-source geothermal systems for elementary facilities, evaluated first-quarter operating performance, and expanded after-school program capacity.

threads.name: Medford High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated formal participation in the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) core program for Medford High School in late 2023 and established a dedicated high school building committee in early 2024. The body appointed an Owner's Project Manager, certified future enrollment capacity, approved the educational plan, and evaluated site alternatives. Work continued through 2026 with design modifications to navigate a property deed restriction, submission of preferred schematic options to the state, and selection of a Construction Manager at Risk delivery method.

threads.name: District Facilities Infrastructure and HVAC Upgrades
threads.summary: Facing widespread cooling failures across aging school buildings, the committee launched capital assessments and approved partial decarbonization plans to replace failing mechanical systems. The body authorized major bond requests to fund comprehensive HVAC replacements at the Andrews and McGlynn schools while executing power purchase agreements for rooftop solar installations. Capital planning broadened following a facilities assessment that identified over $83 million in needed repairs district-wide, leading to schematic design approvals and geothermal heat pump selection for elementary facilities.

threads.name: Superintendent Leadership and Evaluation
threads.summary: The committee performed composite annual performance reviews and set district improvement goals for Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent. Following contract negotiations and Dr. Edouard-Vincent's departure in early 2025, the committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent. In early 2026, after reviewing Dr. Galusi's transitional leadership performance and district entry findings, the committee formally appointed her as permanent superintendent and executed a three-year contract.

threads.name: Elementary School Capacity and Space Utilization
threads.summary: Severe enrollment imbalances and space constraints—notably at Roberts Elementary School—prompted staff and community requests for redistricting and space utilization planning. To alleviate immediate overcrowding, the committee approved relocating early education classrooms and evaluated proposals to reconfigure elementary and middle school grade spans. The body subsequently voted to delay middle school reconfigurations until 2028 while continuing to refine intra-district enrollment and reassignment policies.

threads.name: Student Transportation and Bus Safety
threads.summary: Vendor bus driver shortages caused route disruptions and overcrowding, leading the committee to conduct community surveys and evaluate transit service alternatives. The body directed route optimizations, requested safety monitoring reports, and approved using internal paraprofessionals as rotating bus monitors. Long-term planning produced a new five-year yellow bus contract, feasibility studies on bus electrification, and expanded high school late bus services.

threads.name: After-School Programming Expansion
threads.summary: High demand and long waitlists for school-age childcare led the committee to request administrative reports and adjust fee structures to sustain operations. The body commissioned a program assessment by the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative to evaluate staffing models and program capacity. Based on these recommendations, the committee implemented multi-day tuition rate cards, converted part-time roles to full-time site directors, and significantly reduced waitlists.

threads.name: Career and Technical Education (CTE) Governance
threads.summary: The committee supported expanding vocational programming at Medford Vocational Technical High School and integrated CTE expansion options into MSBA building studies. To handle high applicant volume in vocational fields, the body updated its admissions framework to establish a non-weighted lottery system in alignment with state guidelines. Vocational offerings were further updated through an honors pilot program that integrates capstone projects and co-op experiences for upperclassmen.

threads.name: District Policy and Educational Governance
threads.summary: The committee routinely updated foundational district policies, adopting new frameworks for bullying prevention, gender identity non-discrimination, and Title IX sexual discrimination grievance procedures. Following state legislative changes that eliminated the MCAS graduation mandate, the body revised high school graduation policies to align competency determinations with coursework. Additionally, the committee passed policies governing generative artificial intelligence in instruction and establishing protocols for immigration law enforcement in school buildings.
